comments.content:
[medium] This rollback can fail when the old function signature is absent—for example, on a fresh install, an already-upgraded database, or a partial upgrade. Use `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS ...` here and in the reverse migration so both directions remain idempotent across those states.

```suggestion
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS @extschema@.add_continuous_aggregate_policy(
    continuous_aggregate REGCLASS,
    start_offset "any",
    end_offset "any",
    schedule_interval INTERVAL,
    if_not_exists BOOL,
    initial_start TIMESTAMPTZ,
    timezone TEXT,
    include_tiered_data BOOL,
    buckets_per_batch INTEGER,
    max_batches_per_execution INTEGER
);
```

[medium] The `refresh_newest_first` assignment should happen inside the following `if (policy_data)` block instead of before it — that's the only place the value is consumed, and moving it avoids pointlessly running the call when `policy_data` is undefined.
[low] A short assertion around `DROP FUNCTION` could make this invariant easier to diagnose during development.
[low] Consider testing `psprintf()` across a transition from an old value to a new one.
